## Cardinalities in finite monoids of G-equivariant functions
# arXiv:2503.03772v1 [math.GR] 4 Mar 2025

blocks.text: Cardinalities in finite monoids of G-equivariant functions

For any group G, a G-set is simply a set X on which G acts; that is, there exists a function · : G × X → X such that e · x = x for all x ∈ X and g · (h · x) = (gh) · x for all x ∈ X, g,h ∈ G In the context of semigroup theory, G-sets are also known as G-acts. A G-equivariant transformation of X, or a G-endomorphism of X, is a function τ : X → X such that τ(g · x) = g · τ(x)for all g ∈ G, x ∈ X. These maps are fundamental in the category of G-sets and find applications in various branches of mathematics such as equivariant topology, representation theory, and statistical inference.
Keywords: Group actions, G-sets, G-equivariant function, cardinality. MSC 2020: 20B25, 20E22, 20M20.

The set of all G-equivariant transformations of X, which are functions that commute with the group action, forms a monoid under function composition. We denote this monoid as EndG(X), and its group of units, consisting of all bijective G-equivariant transformations, as AutG(X). These objects have been extensively studied in various contexts (see [2], [3], [10], [16]).
